title: Touring with Billie Holiday and the crooked bus
summary: Jones describes the one-nighters, the band's poor bus that was swapped for a good one near New York, so they looked like a big act.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Did she ever sing with your band, Mitzi Green?
Of course not, no. I just mentioned it as an aside, during that particular period. But Lady Day was with us.
What were some of the tours like? Did Lady Day make any tours with you? Did she travel with you?
She did not make any tunes with the band.
Oh sure, she made the tours. She was on the road, she made theatres, she made one-nighters with us.
What were the one-nighters like, Jo, in the theatres?
Well, we took it with a grain of salt -
We just got through with this "take it with a grain of salt" and I was interrupted... I was asking
what were the tours like and you said you took it with a grain of salt. Now you can go on with that.

Milt, as you know, you were with Cab Calloway, you, and you didn't have to stay at Mother's Lunch like we did, see, because we were still in a Lert's bus. You guys were on a train; we hadn't got to that plateau then and we had this crooked bus that went down the highway crooked. That's right, I have a picture I can show you coming out of Pittsburgh. This bus used to go down the highway sideways and Mr. Lert, to make us look like a big act, used to send over a good bus from Newark and from the Woodside. He put all our stuff in there and then just as we come out of the tunnel where you got to the airport, then we'd exchange buses and get this crooked bus. I think that was 15 or 20¢ a mile; we could not afford it with the Kay Kyser and you guys. So then when we come back into New York off our little tour, then we'd have the crooked bus they'd take the good bus and come in, and we looked like a big act, because it was short mileage and everyone thought we were on big time, you see. That means that I'm going into a thing that's in Miss Billie Holiday's book and there was various things, since we're speaking about this particular thing, because we can't leave this out. Billie was left-handed and she never shot dice in her life. Lester Young had one dollar and he said, "Come on, Billie, shoot this dollar for me."
